Hi Markus,

Thanks for the redlines. Before we pull legal in, two quick asks from procurement & security so we can map the order form to our internal controls:

We have a short window this week to get the DPA into our signature packet. If you can share a one-page summary plus the evidence sheet, I can escalate to our security reviewer.

Appreciate it,
Emma

Thanks Emma — looping in our privacy lead and contracts SME. Quick answers up front:

- EU-only flow: we can offer EU-only residency for the production tenant and commit to routing EU data to EU regions for that tenant. Fallbacks to US-hosted replicas are negotiable but will require explicit tiering in the Order Form.
- Evidence: attaching a starter evidence matrix (novaprod_evidence_matrix.xlsx) and a Word file with my suggested Order Form language for the hosting carveout.

Irene / Ben — could you review the attached matrix and confirm the SCC implementation notes and whether we should mark the KMS approach as "customer-managed (optional)" or "Redwood-managed with BYOK" in the Order Form? Also flag any DPA redlines we should preemptively accept vs escalate.

Next steps I propose:
- Internal quick sync (15m) today to align on KMS option + fallback routing language.
- Send the one-page summary back to Emma with the evidence sheet and proposed redline bullets.

Markus
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

On Wed, May 21, 2025 at 10:05 AM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> - EU-only flow: we can offer EU-only residency for the production tenant and commit to routing EU data to EU regions for that tenant.
> - Evidence: attaching a starter evidence matrix and suggested Order Form language.

Thanks — quick notes from privacy:

1) SCCs: We should reference the updated EU standard clauses (post-2021 mechanism) and include a clear fall-back path: "In the event of unavoidable cross-border routing, Redwood will notify and provide mitigation (encryption at rest + KMS controls)". That language reduces procurement pushback.
2) Roles: For Novaprod, propose controller/processor split in the DPA as currently drafted but add an explicit subprocessor approval layer for EU tenant exports.
3) KMS: Offer BYOK as optional; default to Redwood-managed KMS with a dedicated Customer Key for EU-only tenants. BYOK requires procurement ops changes and will affect lead time and pricing.

I can draft a short paragraph for the DPA and a checklist for the evidence matrix (SOC2 report pointer, retention policy doc, sample audit log snippet, subprocessor roster). Markus — I will add these to the spreadsheet and return.

Irene Choi
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Quoted-by: "Emma Lowe <emma.lowe@novaprod.com>"

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lowe <emma.lowe@novaprod.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 May 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosting routing + evidence preflight for Order Form

Emma — thanks for the note. I reviewed Markus and Irene's points and attached a cleaned redline (orderform_redline_v2.docx) and a short "what we can commit" bullet list below we can send back to you this afternoon: 

1) Commitment: EU-only data residency for Novaprod's production tenant; all writes/read replicas for that tenant will be provisioned in EU regions.
2) Fallbacks: In extraordinary operational emergencies we may route to US replicas for read-only failover; such events require prior notice and escalation to Novaprod security.
3) SCCs & DPA: We will adopt the EU SCCs (controller->processor) and provide an annex with subprocessor list and SOC2 pointer.
4) KMS: Default Redwood-managed KMS using a dedicated Customer Key for EU tenants; BYOK optional at additional cost and lead time.

I'll send the one-page summary and the evidence matrix to you now (linked). If that looks good I'll get legal to sign off on the DPA redlines and push to DocuSign (envelope id above).

Best,
Ben Carter
Contracts Lead, Redwood Inference
